column3: Directly parallels disbelief, opposition to the messenger, and guidance made clear beforehand.
Adds the arrival of a manifest messenger as a condition of later recollection.
States guidance for believers, but adds little to the post-witness reversal.
Pairs the call to Islam with the same refusal of guidance for wrongdoers.
Frames messenger, assent, witnessing, and support within a binding covenant.
Contrasts the focus's wrongdoing with faith kept free of wrongdoing and consequent guidance.
Joins testimony, post-oath accountability, and the refusal of guidance to the defiantly disobedient.
Keeps the immediate address on rejecting Allah's signs under divine witness.
Offers the positive movement from darkness toward paths of peace.
Links the messenger's delivery of revelation to the refusal of guidance for disbelievers.
Names the straight path but is redundant after more specific guidance cards.
Places guided and defiantly disobedient responses among the inheritors of prophethood and scripture.
Specifies disbelief after faith and an increase in disbelief, sharpening the focus's reversal.
Makes turning away after the covenant the mark of defiantly disobedient people.
Shows trust in future divine guidance without the focus's evidentiary reversal.
Contrasts the One who guides to truth with those unable to guide themselves.
Sets the prior surrounding confession of all revelation and messengers against later disbelief.
Parallels the formula that Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient.
Identifies concealing clear proofs and guidance after their clarification as blameworthy.
Shows Abraham chosen and guided to a straight path as a distant positive contrast.
Connects clear signs with Allah's guidance, though without the rejection sequence.
Joins messengers, clear proofs, disagreement after them, and guidance of believers to truth.
Extends the immediate passage's contrast between seeking another religion and universal submission.
Provides a contrary claim to guide, exposing a human claim over against divine guidance.
Pairs a decisive sign confronting disbelief with Allah's refusal to guide wrongdoers.
Continues the nearby call to follow Abraham's upright way.
States that the Qur'an guides to what is most upright, without the focus's deliberate reversal.
Makes prior guidance and clarification precede any judgment of going astray.
The collective boast of support adds no clear element to the focus.
Names following desire without divine guidance and repeats the refusal of guidance for wrongdoers.
Adds oath-breaking and intent against the messenger as active repudiation.
Defines seeking a religion other than Islam as unaccepted in the immediate context.
Affirms Allah as the continuing guide in a general form.
Uses slipping after clear proofs as a close structural parallel.
Directly follows the passage with blocking believers from Allah's path while being witnesses.
Associates belief and devoted practice with hoped-for guidance.
Places clear proofs given to messengers beside later division into believers and disbelievers.
The exception for devoted servants does not clarify the focus's stated condition.
Affirms future guidance from the Creator as a broad contrast.
Shows a moment when belief no longer benefits disbelievers.
Supplies the immediate consequence assigned to the people described in the focus.
Provides a contrary guide who misleads his people rather than guiding them.
Combines denial of signs, self-witness, and being disbelievers.
Restates the focus's "how can you disbelieve" with signs recited and the messenger present.
Distinguishes claimed submission from Allah's guidance to faith.
Names witnesses and contrasts believers with wrongdoers, but shifts to affliction.
Continues the Abrahamic path without the focus's witness and rejection structure.
The request for clarification in the cattle narrative has no focused addition here.
Adds the coming of a noble messenger in a different narrative setting.
Warns believers that obedience to some People of the Book can return them to disbelief after faith.
States that refusing Allah's signs is bound to not being guided.
Shows faith increasing with faith, a broad reverse movement to the focus.
The designation of wise book-verses adds no distinct element.
Names following desires without knowledge and repeats no guidance for wrongdoers.
Links disbelief in the truth brought to them with expelling the messenger and loss of the path.
Supplies a nearby declaration of guidance for all worlds, but not the reversal.
Names guidance and reminder in a general, redundant form.
Joins Islam, the messenger as witness, and the community's witnessing role.
Shows inherited scripture, studied covenant, and failure to uphold what was known.
Connects guidance to Moses with scripture inherited by Israel.
Shows the end of wrongdoers without adding the focus's path of prior witness.
Continues the nearby outcome for those who remain disbelievers.
Distinguishes those astray from those guided, but lacks the focus's evidentiary sequence.
Shows belief becoming unavailing only after overwhelming punishment is seen.
Combines the messenger's call to faith with a taken covenant.
Calls the Qur'an guidance and mercy for believers in general terms.
Affirms Allah's true promise but has only a remote link through truth.
Adds the self-description of a trustworthy messenger.
Names clear perceptions, guidance, and mercy for those with certainty.
Links messengers reciting signs, warning, and self-witness that the hearers were disbelievers.
The recording of secret speech does not add to the focus.
Associates scripture and criterion with hoped-for guidance.
The statement about not valuing Allah rightly is too indirect here.
Marks divine guidance as beyond even the messenger's personal power.
The sea-distress narrative adds no specific understanding of the focus.
Distinguishes outward looking at the messenger from being able to guide the unseeing.
The command to endure against those without certainty is too indirect.
Makes obeying the messenger the stated path to guidance and limits his task to clear delivery.
The command to forgive those not awaiting Allah's days has no focused link.
Contrasts faith that brings guidance with turning away into dissension.
Gives a prior pattern of demanding more after clear proofs and then turning to the calf.
Keeps repentance, faith, righteous action, and then guidance as a possible counter-trajectory.
Describes denying what was not encompassed in knowledge and names the end of wrongdoers.
Shows the same sign becoming guidance or misguidance according to the recipient's stance.
Joins recited signs with arrogant rejection and criminal identity.
States that Allah does not guide treacherous plotting, only a distant parallel.
The transfer of inheritance to another people adds no clear link.
Counters the later claim that guidance had never reached the speaker.
The assertion of certain truth alone is too general.
States the impossibility of finding a path for one Allah has led astray.
Addresses collective ingratitude but not the focus's witnessed messenger and proofs.
Shows a responsive posture when signs are recited, as a broad contrast.
Shows the foreclosed excuse that no messenger and signs had come to them.
Presents written guidance and mercy for those who revere Allah.
The conduct instruction and call to repentance do not illuminate the focus.
Names guidance and mercy for those who do good.
The discovery and concealment of Joseph has no relevant link.
Associates confirmation and detailed exposition with guidance for believers.
The creation-and-replacement statement adds no focused evidence.
Contrasts names and desire with guidance that has already come from their Lord.
Adds the immediate exception of repentance, reform, and divine forgiveness after the focus's judgment.
Names exchanging faith for disbelief as leaving the even way.
Describes the wish to turn believers back to disbelief after their faith.
States the consequence of turning back from religion and dying in disbelief.
Names the exchange of disbelief for faith and its loss.
Shows hearing a caller to faith and answering with belief, the positive counterpart to witnessed rejection.
Joins opposing the messenger with following another way after guidance has become clear.
Makes disbelief in Allah, His messengers, books, and the Last Day a manifest going astray.
Directly traces repeated belief and disbelief, ending in no forgiveness or guidance to a way.
Addresses those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers while trying to divide between them.
Combines disbelief and barring from Allah's path with far-going error.
States that those who disbelieve and wrong cannot be forgiven or guided to a path.
Pairs failure to judge by what Allah sent down with the designation of disbelievers.
Pairs wrongdoing with failure to judge by what Allah sent down.
Pairs defiant disobedience with failure to judge by what Allah sent down.
Repeats that Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people within a warning about allegiance.
Links refusal to uphold inherited revelation with increase in transgression and disbelief.
Names disbelief in a claim concerning the Messiah and reports his call to worship Allah.
Distinguishes the messenger's grief from wrongdoers' denial of Allah's signs.
Shows turning from signs, refusing the right path, and taking the path of error instead.
Identifies persistent disbelievers who do not believe at all.
Explicitly says that they disbelieved after their faith.
Explicitly says that they disbelieved after their Islam.
Shows later denial of signs after messengers brought clear proofs.
Locates belief under Allah's permission and places defilement on those who do not use reason.
Sets Allah's leaving astray beside His guidance of whoever turns to Him.
Sets the mission of every community beside those Allah guides and those for whom error is due.
States that Allah does not guide one whom He leaves astray.
Defines the guided and the astray by Allah's guidance and states no protector besides Him for the latter.
Defines the rightly guided as one Allah guides and the astray as lacking a guiding protector.
Promises that following divine guidance prevents going astray and misery.
Shows doubt after clear proofs, then settled disbelief after a messenger's passing.
Contrasts guidance offered to Thamud with their preference for blindness over guidance.
Calls revelation guidance and healing for believers while describing others as deaf and blind to it.
Shows the reverse course: those already guided receive increased guidance and their guarding awareness.
Directly names turning back after guidance has become clear to them.
Combines disbelief, barring from Allah's path, and dying as disbelievers.
Shows a people's deviation after a messenger's address and Allah's not guiding defiantly disobedient people.
